title: Pilot experiments
outcome: Explain pilot experiments using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: A pilot tests the procedure. A pilot checks whether the team can score answers consistently before running the main study.
given: Two reviewers score four practice answers. They agree on three and disagree on one; these answers are excluded from final evaluation.

steps.label: Try the workflow
steps.detail: Both reviewers apply the draft rubric to four practice answers.

steps.label: Repair the rubric
steps.detail: Discuss the disagreement and clarify the scoring rule before the main run.

explanation: A pilot can reveal missing instructions, practical delays or ambiguous scoring. It is preparation, not an untouched final estimate after the team uses it to revise methods.

counterfactual.change: Add the corrected pilot answers into final evaluation.
counterfactual.prediction: Declare them previously exposed rather than untouched final evidence.
counterfactual.reason: Rubric development already used those answers.

student_task: Calculate reviewer agreement on the four pilot answers. What can the disagreement improve, and why are those revised practice answers not untouched final evidence?
teacher_answer: Both reviewers apply the draft rubric to four practice answers. Agreement is 3/4=75% on this pilot. Discuss the disagreement and clarify the scoring rule before the main run. Changed case: Declare them previously exposed rather than untouched final evidence. Rubric development already used those answers.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: Four pilot answers do not establish long-run reviewer reliability or a stable performance effect.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
